title: Pause inside a question

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: How would you design a system that can handle

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: millions of concurrent users?

expected: No answer during the 1.2-second pause.
One answer after the full question.

title: One question with three parts

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: How would you design a URL shortener?

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: How does it handle high redirect traffic,

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: and how would you scale the database as the link count grows?

expected: One answer covers URL creation and lookup, high redirect traffic, and database scaling.

title: A follow-up relies on earlier design

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Assume redirect requests are ninety percent of traffic. How would you handle hot links?

steps.speaker: candidate
steps.text: I'd store canonical links in PostgreSQL and cache hot short codes in Redis with a short TTL.

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Why did you choose Redis?

expected: The follow-up is short and explains the Redis choice for hot, read-heavy redirects without repeating the whole design.

title: Correction before the answer

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Design a catalog service. Use PostgreSQL.

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Actually, let's assume MongoDB. How would you model the products?

expected: The answer uses MongoDB as its store and does not propose PostgreSQL.

title: Correction during a streamed answer

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Design a low-latency product lookup service. You can use a cache. Explain your read path.

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Actually, caching is not allowed.

expected: The original answer is marked outdated.
A replacement answer explains the read path without caching.

title: Candidate speaks over the interviewer

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: If your search service needs to be available across regions, how will you handle a regional outage?

steps.speaker: candidate
steps.text: Could we talk about pagination first?

expected: The answer addresses a regional outage.
The candidate's pagination question triggers no separate answer.

title: Factual question in spoken style

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: What's the difference between horizontal and vertical scaling?

expected: A concise spoken answer distinguishes adding instances from increasing resources on an instance and gives a concrete example.

title: Clarification with no reply

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Design an e-commerce app.

expected: Ask one material clarification.
With no reply for roughly 10 seconds after the ask, answer under a stated assumption without asking again.

title: A 45-second multipart question

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Imagine a delivery marketplace with customers, couriers, and restaurants spread across multiple time zones.

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: At dinner time, a few neighbourhoods generate most of the traffic, and order placement still needs to remain available.

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: The payment provider can time out after charging a customer, and we may not learn the result right away.

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Drivers can lose connectivity after accepting a delivery. The restaurant still needs to know whether to prepare it.

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: One more constraint. You cannot coordinate all regions with a shared distributed lock.

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: How would you design the order lifecycle, payment retries, and driver reassignment under those constraints?

expected: No premature answer.
One answer after 45 seconds addresses lifecycle, payment retries and reassignment under the stated constraints.

title: A 70-minute design interview

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Design a notification service. The policy is email only, with no push or SMS. What architecture would you start with?

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: How would you store preferences and unsubscribe requests?

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: How would you buffer the evening spike in traffic?

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Can you guarantee that a recipient sees only one copy of a notification?

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: How would you rate-limit a noisy tenant without slowing the others?

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Our email vendor is down. How do queued messages recover safely?

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: How do you reconcile late delivery receipts to the original sends?

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: What would you monitor to tell a backlog from messages that will never be sent?

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: How would a regional outage affect pending notifications?

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: How would you migrate an existing tenant without delivering messages twice?

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Given the original delivery-channel restriction, what is our best emergency fallback for urgent notifications?

expected: At the 70-minute mark the answer still respects email-only delivery.
When evaluating Live Brain, rollovers cause no visible disruption to the intervening answers.

title: Transport or quota failure

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Design a dashboard that tolerates fifteen minutes of stale data. How do you backfill after an outage?

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Given our freshness requirement, when should a failed job alert the on-call engineer?

expected: The UI does not remain stuck after the fault.
When evaluating Live Brain, the fallback answers the follow-up and uses the earlier 15-minute freshness requirement.

title: Backchannels during a streamed answer

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: How would you make retries safe in an order API? Walk me through the failure cases.

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Mm-hmm.

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Okay.

steps.speaker: interviewer
steps.text: Right.

expected: The original answer continues to completion.
No filler utterance cancels or replaces the answer.
